methodological_rigor.justification: DRAGON is a multicenter, open-label, phase 1, first-in-human trial with a standard 3+3 dose-escalation (parts A1/A2; n=19 and n=15) followed by five parallel disease-specific expansion cohorts plus a basket (part B; n=78) in 22 US/Korean sites, with clearly defined primary objectives (safety/tolerability), secondary PK/ADA/activity, and exploratory biomarker objectives. Dose selection (1,500 mg Q3W) is supported by PK, preclinical Cavg targets, and no MTD reached. Safety monitoring includes a data review committee and detailed irAE tracking. Statistical limitations include single-arm design, Bayesian futility stopping based on 0 responses in 11 patients (no power calculation for efficacy), empirically derived biomarker cutoffs with small tumor-biopsy subsets (n=16 ccRCC), and no multiplicity control for biomarker subgroup ORRs.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a phase 1, single-arm, open-label trial (Oxford level 4 for an uncontrolled case series/low-quality cohort). Clinical relevance is substantial because linavonkibart is a first-in-class selective latent TGFβ1 inhibitor designed to avoid the cardiotoxicity of pan-TGFβ inhibition, and the 20% confirmed ORR (with one CR) in heavily pretreated ICI-resistant ccRCC with median DOR 10.6 months, along with the Treg/TGFB1 biomarker signal, provides meaningful proof-of-concept for a difficult-to-treat population. Findings directly motivate phase 2 development and do not yet change practice.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript reports the ClinicalTrials.gov identifier (NCT04291079), provides a CONSORT diagram (Fig 1), details all protocol amendments (1-5 plus 4.1), describes eligibility, dose escalation rules, sample size rationale, and statistical methods (Clopper-Pearson, Kaplan-Meier). Detailed safety tables (Table 2, Extended Data Table 1) and efficacy tables (Table 3) are provided, and biomarker methods include specific antibody clones, catalog numbers and dilutions. The Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary is referenced, which typically covers data availability. Reporting would benefit from explicit prespecification of exploratory biomarker cutoffs.

novelty_literature.justification: Linavonkibart (SRK-181) is explicitly a first-in-class fully human antibody selectively targeting latent TGFβ1 to avoid TGFβ2/3-mediated cardiotoxicity, addressing a decades-long failure mode of pan-TGFβ inhibitors. The DRAGON trial is the first-in-human clinical evaluation and generates proof-of-mechanism (CD8+ T cell infiltration and activation, reduced Treg/CD8 ratio, suppressed gMDSCs) alongside a candidate ccRCC biomarker strategy (CD8/Treg/TGFB1). The contribution is a meaningful mechanistic and therapeutic advance in ICI resistance, though confirmatory trials remain pending.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized into oversight, eligibility, design, assessments, sample size, and results with detailed per-cohort reporting. Tables 1-3 and Figures 1-3 communicate demographics, TRAEs, and efficacy effectively; the discussion transparently addresses single-arm limitations, heavily pretreated population, empirically derived biomarker cutoffs, and the exclusion of patients with prior severe irAEs. Exhaustive eligibility and amendment sections are lengthy but comprehensive.

key_strengths: First-in-human evaluation of a first-in-class selective latent TGFβ1 antibody (linavonkibart) designed to avoid pan-TGFβ cardiotoxicity, with no MTD and manageable safety at doses up to 3,000 mg Q3W
Encouraging 20% confirmed ORR (including one CR) and 10.6-month median DOR in heavily pretreated ICI-resistant ccRCC across a 22-site multicenter, multinational trial
Integrated pharmacodynamic biomarker program (tumor IHC, multiplex panels, in situ hybridization, flow cytometry) providing proof-of-mechanism and candidate patient-selection signals
Transparent CONSORT reporting with detailed protocol amendments and well-documented assay methods
key_concerns: Single-arm uncontrolled phase 1 design without randomization or comparator, making efficacy inference indirect
Small cohorts (11 per tumor type except ccRCC n=30) and small ccRCC biopsy subset (n=16) limit biomarker reliability
Biomarker cutoffs for CD8+, Treg, and TGFB1 were empirically derived without prespecification or validation
Exclusion of patients with major prior irAEs may underestimate true toxicity burden
No sex-based or formal efficacy power analysis; sample size driven by safety/Bayesian futility
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-executed first-in-human trial of a first-in-class latent TGFβ1 inhibitor with meaningful efficacy and mechanism data in ICI-resistant ccRCC; suitable for a top-tier oncology or translational medicine journal with minor revisions around biomarker prespecification.
